turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, my regular doctor is the one who told me to come see you. He says I've gotten too thin. I mean, I can see what he means—my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me at my cleaning job lately. But, if I'm being honest, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and the number is lower.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient acknowledges significant weight loss and being told by their doctor that they have gotten too thin, noting that their work pants are hanging loose.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from feeling relieved when you see a lower number, do you have an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though others say you're thin?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I suppose I do. It's... well, if I eat something heavier, you know, like biscuits or a plate of pasta, I spend the rest of the day just scared that it's going to show on me. I end up checking myself in the mirror a lot, and I just can't stop thinking that I need to find a way to make up for eating it.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient confirms having an intense fear of gaining weight, stating they spend the rest of the day scared it will show on them after eating heavier foods.

turns.doctor_question: When you say you try to 'make up for' eating something like pasta, what exactly do you do—do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively afterward?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or anything like that. I'm on my feet a lot for work, cleaning and moving around, but I don't go out and exercise for hours on purpose. I just... I might skip my next meal, or I just try to eat a lot less the next day to balance it out.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient reports skipping meals or eating significantly less the following day to compensate for eating food like pasta, which represents non-purging compensatory behavior (fasting).
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies self-induced vomiting and the use of laxatives to prevent weight gain.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me your current height and weight, and how that compares to what you weighed before you started losing weight?
turns.patient_response:
Well... I'm honestly not sure of the exact numbers. I haven't had my height measured in a long time, so I couldn't tell you that for sure. 

And with my weight, even though I check the scale, I don't really keep track of the exact number in my head. I just look to make sure it's going down. I don't really know exactly what I weighed before I started losing, either. I just know it's a lot less now than it used to be.

symptom_reasoning.S026: The patient confirms significant weight loss by stating that their current weight is 'a lot less now than it used to be' and that they actively check to ensure it continues to go down.
